title: Handbook sweep: the logs section and two overcorrected claims
action: SECOND REVISION. The previous round closed four of six truths; two FAILs remain and both were found by READING, not by grepping — which is the lesson of this cell. (1) THE FOURTH BLIND SPOT, and the one that matters: docs/handbook/register.md:329 still says .bee/logs/test-results.json is 'Written by `bee test`, read by `cells finish` and `bee close`', and :333-335 still says .bee/logs/test-failure-<runner>-<index>.log holds 'the complete output of a failing declared command, one file per (runner, index) where runner is `test`, `finish` or `close`'. Both name finish and close as runners of the declared command. The code says otherwise: verbs/test_runner.rs emits only the `test` runner name, and the only runtime reader of test-results.json is the red-base check in verbs/cells/handlers_write.rs (`cells claim`); verbs/cells/finish_support.rs comments that `bee test` is now the only writer, and verbs/drivers/close.rs mentions the path only in a comment. Neither the old single-line grep nor the new multiline pattern covers this phrasing — that is exactly why the cell now demands reading the section, not matching it. (2) TWO OVERCORRECTIONS from the last round: docs/handbook/overview.md:124-125 and docs/handbook/stages/swarming.md:70-71 both say merge checks the proof line 'against the staged merge' — a leftover from the boundary-run sentence. verbs/worktree/phases.rs makes it a ZERO-MUTATION precondition run BEFORE any bookkeeping commit, so a proof-less merge is refused and never staged at all. And docs/handbook/overview.md:136-138 says 'a capped cell with no valid proof line refuses the close/merge door' — verbs/cells/proof.rs passes a cap with NO trace.report at all as legacy, ungated; only a cap that HAS a report with a bad tests value refuses. METHOD, and this is the whole point of the round: read every passage in the three files that mentions tests, proof, the doors, or the logs, and check each claim against the source. Do not pattern-hunt — two rounds of grepping already missed these. UNCHANGED: docs/handbook/register.md:203-209 (correct historical labelling, citing decision 13ce1858), docs/handbook/architecture-map.md and docs/handbook/stages/executing.md (both verified correct by the judge this round), docs/specs/test-simple.md, docs/history/**, .bee/cells/archive/**, docs/codebase-overview.md, .bee/config-sample.json, and everything under packages/.

Every claim about tests, proof, the doors, or the logs in the three touched files was checked against the source, and the cap says which passages were read rather than matched.
